meta.title: NotPetya Ransomware CAD Model
meta.description: A model of the 2017 worldwide attack by the Sanworm Team using the NotPetya Ransomware
meta.article: NotPetya is malware that was used by Sandworm Team in a worldwide attack starting on June 27, 2017. While NotPetya appears as a form of ransomware, its main purpose was to destroy data and disk structures on compromised systems; the attackers never intended to make the encrypted data recoverable.

data.label: Local Execution & Spread
user_properties:
Once the malware was downloaded onto a computer, it attempted to escalate its privileges and determine whether antivirus processes were running.
The malware then attempted to identify other computers on the same network. The malware would attempt to extract and execute a credential stealing 
program and/or escalate its privileges to achieve lateral movement to other computers on the network. If execution failed, the malware spread itself to 
other victim computers using either the exploit EtemalBlue or EternalRomance for SMBv1 to connect to other network nodes without credentials, then 
copy itself to those nodes and attempt to execute. After attempting lateral movement within the compromised computer's network, the malware searched
 for files ending with dozens of different file extensions and began encrypting those files on the compromised computer. Once the files were encrypted,
 the malware created a text file containing the ransom note inside every folder that contained encrypted files.

data.label: Initial Access
user_properties:
The NotPetya malware was disseminated initially using a popular Ukrainian accounting 
software called M.E.Doc. The software was periodically updated through an update 
server (the "Update Server"). The attackers rerouted internet traffic from the Update Server 
to their France-based server which delivered the malware to the victim computers. The 
attackers surreptitiously add malicious functionality to the files containing the software 
updates (the "Update Files") and computers receiving M.E.Doc software updates downloaded 
these Update Files, which at some point included the NotPetya malware.

data.label: Overview
user_properties:
On June 27, 2017 the malicious actors executed a
series of malware attacks to render the computer 
systems used by Ukrainian organizations inoperable, 
including banks, newspapers, and electricity companies. 
The "NotPetya" malware was used to target the electric 
sector. The NotPetya malware spread to connected 
networks belonging to other victim computer systems 
belonging to victims in other countries, including in 
the United States.
